title: When the Wardrobe Burns
premise: Orsen Quintana, a night librarian who has spent decades cataloguing silences instead of speaking his own, is asked by Mirela Voss—the last fluent speaker of Vessic, a dying trade-tongue of dockworkers and deserters—to become her final student. As he learns the language, he uncovers that Mirela once testified falsely to protect the found family that raised him, and that his own father's disappearance is tangled in her lie. When developers move to demolish her harbor house and the city refuses to hear her, Orsen must choose between the loyalty of silence and the justice of speech, recording her true testimony and burning the wardrobe that holds his own unsaid letters. In the end, he says goodbye aloud in Vessic at her deathbed, becomes the language's last speaker himself, and opens the library after hours as a school for the city's unspoken things.
about_author: Bram Delacroix is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent twelve years cataloguing the papers of defunct shipping guilds along a fading coastline. Their fiction explores languages on the edge of extinction and the people who keep secrets as a form of love.

chapters.title: The Inventory of Unsaid Things
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. We meet the night library, his habit of recording what patrons almost say, and the locked wardrobe of letters he has never mailed. Emotional beat: comfortable loneliness beginning to chafe.

chapters.title: A Woman Who Counts in Vessic
chapters.summary: Mirela Voss appears at the desk at 3 a.m., speaking a language no catalog recognizes, and asks Orsen to be her last student. He refuses out of fear; she leaves a Vessic counting rhyme behind. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: Lessons at the Edge of the Harbor
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He begins secret lessons in Mirela's condemned harbor house, learning that Vessic has no word for 'alone'—only 'unaccompanied, temporarily.' Emotional beat: the first warmth of found family.

chapters.title: The Wardrobe Hums
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, intercut with his dead father's letters. Studying Vessic unlocks memories; he realizes his father spoke it, and that Mirela's name appears in one unsent letter. Emotional beat: dread beneath tenderness.

chapters.title: What Mirela Swore
chapters.summary: Mirela's POV. A confession chapter: decades ago she gave false testimony to shield a crew of deserters—including Orsen's father—from a fatal dock fire inquiry. Emotional beat: guilt worn as loyalty.

chapters.title: Demolition Notices
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The city posts eviction orders; the found family of old dockworkers scatters to defend the house. Orsen must decide whether exposing Mirela's lie could save it or destroy everyone. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth sharpening into a blade.

chapters.title: The Hearing Nobody Attends
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. At a city hearing, official channels fail; Mirela's testimony is ruled inadmissible because Vessic isn't a 'recognized' language. Emotional beat: the law's cold arithmetic against human memory.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He records Mirela's full true testimony in Vessic and broadcasts it through the library's night frequency, letting the dockworkers' descendants hear the fire's real story. Emotional beat: speech as act of love; the wardrobe begins to burn in his mind.

chapters.title: Goodbye, Out Loud
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, climax. Mirela is dying; he finally burns the wardrobe of unsent letters, reads his father's last words aloud, and speaks his goodbye to her in fluent Vessic as she corrects his grammar one final time, gently. Emotional beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: The Night School
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, resolution. The harbor house is lost, but its people gather in the library after hours; Orsen, now the last speaker, teaches Vessic to anyone who can't sleep. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into inheritance and quiet hope.
